U.S. FUEL PRICES have risen sharply since the start of the year as simultaneous wars with Iran and between Russia and Ukraine have disrupted the global refining system. Retail gasoline prices (including taxes) are up by more than 40% compared with January while diesel prices have risen by more than 50%. In real terms, gasoline and diesel prices are now well above the long-term average having started the year significantly below it. Crude prices turn lower from a five-week high, supporting risk appetite in stocks, while bonds and gold also trade higher. The reversal appears to have been triggered by comments from US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, who said more than 17 million barrels of oil flowed through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, and that it represented the highest level of crude transit since the Iran war reduced flows. Adding to the more constructive tone, Chinese President Xi Jinping said China is willing to work with Middle Eastern countries to “safeguard” shipping through key regional waterways.

The sharp reversal highlights a market where trader conviction remains low, particularly when it comes to holding long positions, with sentiment and prices liable to turn on a dime in response to any comment suggesting an improvement or deterioration in regional flows.
